doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Philadelphia Musical Academy and a mail-boy job at Acme
summary: He studied at the Philadelphia Musical Academy, played a Ray Brown solo, then worked as a mail boy at Acme Markets.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And you just read it off and that’s it. I didn’t care too much, like I said, for the rock music because it was based on the blues, it was very simplistic [scats]. I said what is that? That’s nothing. But now it’s much better because you have better musicians playing it. More creativity and people that know something about music that have put their input, their compositional skills into rock and it sounds better. Sure. So I stayed with my four to the bar. And it seemed as if I’ve gotten more requests for that than anything else. One day I was in Philadelphia, I’d gone to college there at the University of the Performing Arts, at that time it was called the Philadelphia Musical Academy. At that school that’s where Andre Watts used to attend and a few other people that reached a high level in music. I went there for a year and a half. And every Thursday they would have somebody perform, like pianists. So they asked me to come up and perform when I was new in the school. So I went and played my Ray Brown solo. And it was the first time they had heard something like that during that time.
Really. This is supposedly a classical institution? Is that right?
It was all classical, yes. It was called the Philadelphia Musical Academy. Before that it was affiliated with the Conservatory.
Is it called the Curtis Institute now?

But we all had the same teachers, you know they’d go from one place to the next you know. And then we had Combs College of Music, they were all the same teachers. So I went and played my bass, my Ray Brown solo. Then after about a year and a half I began to have a — get a job at Acme Markets, a food chain, worked in the main office as a mail boy. I had a kid and a wife and they paid me $48 a week. So I was working gigs at night, in Read — not Reading.
